videos.script: A variable has three properties beyond its type. When it gets its first value, where its name can be used, and how long it exists. This lesson takes them in that order. {{fine}} First, Java refuses to read a local variable that might not have a value yet. The compiler follows every path through the code, and one bad path is enough. {{defaults}} Fields are different. They start with a default, zero or false or null, which looks just like real data. {{scope}} Then scope. A name declared inside a block ends at its closing brace, and Java will not let two locals in one method share a name. {{stack}} Last, lifetime. Every call gets a frame on a stack, and its locals die with it. A method that calls itself forever fills the stack, and you will count how many frames fit. By the end you can read a compile error about a variable and know which of the three rules it is.
